limits: The material is not identified. The spectrum has only two strong non-substrate modes (206.5 and 471.5 cm-1). The remaining features (270, 296, 323, 403, 684, 910, 957, 996, 1065 cm-1) are at or near the noise level (about 530 counts per point, comparable to their heights), so their positions and widths are uncertain and their presence is not secure.

No reference spectra, literature peak tables or database were consulted, so no mode can be assigned to a specific material, symmetry or irrep. All non-Si assignments are 'unassigned' rather than literature-backed.
No polarization or angle-resolved data, so symmetry (irrep) and polarization pattern cannot be assessed.
The spectrum covers only 60-1100 cm-1, so low-frequency shear and breathing modes (below 60 cm-1) and any higher-frequency modes are not measured.
The two strongest modes alone do not distinguish between candidate layered materials.
No cosmic-ray spikes were detected: the single-point outlier test found no isolated spikes, and the largest 5-point residual (at 471.7 cm-1) sits inside a broad, real peak.
Peak widths for the weak features (270, 296, 684, 910, 957, 1065 cm-1) are at or near the fit bounds, so their FWHM values are not reliable.
Possible second-order Si bands near 300 and about 930-1000 cm-1 could contribute to the weak features in the 290-1000 cm-1 range, but I did not model them separately.
The working-folder name was not used as evidence for the identification.
Measurement conditions (532 nm, 295 K, backscattering, SiO2/Si substrate) were taken from the metadata and not checked against the data.
